newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto's husband being tortured, father says.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto's husband being tortured, father says.

text.p: Ousted Pakistani prime minister Benazir Bhutto's husband, Asif Ali Zardari, is being tortured in detention, his father said on Monday.
"The fact is that he (Zardari) is being tortured before any case is made out against him," Hakim Ali Zardari, a former deputy in the National Assembly (lower house), told reporters.
He did not say how he knew that his son, detained after President Farooq Leghari sacked Bhutto's government on charges of corruption and misrule on November 5, was being mistreated.

Asif Ali Zardari, who was investment minister in his wife's cabinet, was picked up in Lahore and taken to Sihala near Islamabad, but was later shifted to Karachi, capital of Sindh provice. His father said he did not know exactly where he was being held.
Sindh provincial government officials were not immediately available for comment.
Zardari has been held without charge under a sweeping Maintenance of Public Order law. The government has said it is preparing charges against him, but has given no details.
His father urged the authorities to produce Zardari in court and said he would not try to flee Pakistan if he were released.
